description:
Send one transactional SMS to a Georgian mobile number. The text comes from a built-in template; there is no free text.

With a test key (sk_test_) nothing is really sent: a simulator answers. These recipients simulate outcomes: +995512345671 rejected (status `failed`); +995512345672 provider unreachable (error `provider_unavailable`: nothing was sent, retry with the same idempotency_key); +995512345673 ambiguous (status `unknown`); +995512345674 accepted, then `undeliverable`. Any other valid number is accepted, then `delivered`, within about 30 seconds. With a live key it sends a real SMS and spends one credit per segment.

Read `message.status` in the result. `submitted`: the provider accepted it, which is not yet delivery to the phone. `failed`: refused; `message.error` says why. `unknown`: it may or may not have been sent, so do not send it again automatically. `replayed: true`: this idempotency_key and request were already processed, and no second SMS was sent. Call get_message to learn the final outcome.

api_key.description: An sk_test_ key, for example from create_test_key. Leave it out to use the key in this MCP server's Authorization header. A live key (sk_live_) is refused here: tool arguments are kept in the conversation, so a live key belongs in the header.

idempotency_key.description: A new unique value (a UUID) for each logical message. Reuse it only to retry the identical request: the retry then returns the original message instead of sending a second SMS.

locale.description: Language of the message: `ka` (Georgian, the default) or `en`.

template.description:
Which message to send. Message text is never free-form: every message is rendered from one of these templates.

- `verification_code` (`code`): Your verification code is {code}. Do not share it with anyone.
- `login_code` (`code`): Your sign-in code is {code}. If you did not request it, ignore this message.
- `password_reset_code` (`code`, `minutes`): Your password reset code is {code}. It expires in {minutes} minutes.

to.description: Recipient in E.164 format: `+9955` followed by eight digits. No other country or format is accepted, and numbers are never normalized on your behalf.

variables.description: Values for the template's placeholders, all as JSON strings. A `code` is 4 to 8 digits; `minutes` is 1 to 999. Values that look like a link, a web address, or a phone number are refused.

name: send_message
title: Send a code by SMS
